skill.name: similarity-search-patterns
skill.description: Implement efficient similarity search with vector databases for semantic search, RAG retrieval, recommendations, and retrieval performance tuning.
skill.summary: Build vector search systems with practical patterns for Pinecone, Qdrant, pgvector, and Weaviate.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, documentation links, local service defaults, and normal database client methods. The review found one real issue: the pgvector metadata filter builds part of a SQL query from unvalidated keys. No prompt injection attempt or malicious marketplace intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unsafe SQL predicate construction in the pgvector metadata filter example.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist supported metadata keys or map user-facing filters to fixed SQL fragments. Never interpolate raw keys into SQL text.

remediation.issue: API key handling guidance is minimal in the Pinecone example.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note telling users to load API keys from a secret manager or environment variable and never commit them.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe SQL Construction in Metadata Filter
semantic_findings.description: The pgvector template appends metadata filter keys directly into a SQL predicate before executing the query. If untrusted keys reach this function, callers could trigger SQL injection or malformed queries even though values use parameters.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code iterates over filter_metadata keys and inserts each key into an f-string SQL fragment. The values are parameterized, but the key itself is not validated or allowlisted.

content.value_statement: Vector search projects need clear choices for indexes, databases, filters, and ranking. This skill provides practical templates for semantic retrieval systems.
actual_capabilities: Explains common vector distance metrics and when to use each one.
Compares flat, HNSW, and IVF plus PQ index patterns for different scale needs.
Provides Python templates for Pinecone, Qdrant, pgvector, and Weaviate.
Shows upsert, search, filtering, deletion, reranking, and hybrid retrieval flows.
Lists production practices for recall measurement, latency tuning, and cost awareness.
limitations: The examples are templates, not a tested package or deployable service.
Credential storage, authentication, and tenant isolation must be added by the user.
Performance settings need benchmarking against the user data and traffic pattern.
The examples focus on Python and common vector databases.

use_cases.title: Plan a RAG Retrieval Layer
use_cases.description: Choose a vector database pattern, index type, and search flow for a document retrieval application.

use_cases.title: Prototype Vector Storage
use_cases.description: Adapt the Pinecone, Qdrant, pgvector, or Weaviate template for document upsert and similarity queries.

use_cases.title: Improve Search Quality
use_cases.description: Add filters, hybrid search, reranking, and recall checks to an existing semantic search system.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Vector Store
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the similarity-search-patterns skill to compare Pinecone, Qdrant, pgvector, and Weaviate for a small RAG prototype. Recommend one option and explain tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Basic Retrieval
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an upsert and similarity search flow for my documents. Include metadata fields, distance metric choice, and top-k retrieval behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Add Hybrid Ranking
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to extend my semantic search design with keyword search, metadata filtering, and reranking. Explain the scoring and evaluation approach.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Search Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use similarity-search-patterns to review my vector search architecture. Check index choice, filter strategy, latency targets, recall measurement, and operational risks.

output_examples.input: I need semantic search for one million support articles with metadata filters.
output_examples.output: Recommended approach: use an HNSW-backed vector database, pre-filter by stable metadata, and measure recall before tuning latency.

output_examples.input: I already use PostgreSQL and want basic RAG retrieval.
output_examples.output: Suggested path: use pgvector for embeddings, add an HNSW index, and combine vector ranking with full-text search where keyword precision matters.

output_examples.input: My search results are relevant but slow at higher top-k values.
output_examples.output: Optimization focus: tune index parameters, reduce candidate sets with filters, cache common queries, and benchmark P95 and P99 latency.

best_practices: Start with a simple index, then tune recall and latency with measured benchmarks.
Use metadata filters carefully to reduce search space before expensive ranking steps.
Evaluate hybrid search and reranking when semantic results miss exact terminology.
anti_patterns: Do not choose a vector database only because it is popular.
Do not tune index parameters without recall and latency measurements.
Do not copy example credential handling into production without secret management.

faq.question: Does this skill create embeddings?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on storing embeddings and retrieving similar vectors after embeddings already exist.

faq.question: Which vector databases does it cover?
faq.answer: It includes templates for Pinecone, Qdrant, pgvector, and Weaviate.

faq.question: Can it help with RAG systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers retrieval patterns used in RAG, including top-k search, filtering, hybrid search, and reranking.

faq.question: Is the code production ready?
faq.answer: No. The examples are starting points and need authentication, error handling, testing, monitoring, and secure configuration.

faq.question: Does it explain index tradeoffs?
faq.answer: Yes. It summarizes exact, graph-based, and quantized index approaches with recall and scale tradeoffs.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
